title: Restore immutable event compatibility
objective: Unblock trusted control validation without rewriting immutable historical events by narrowly accepting only audited already-published malformed event identities/classes at the V2.1 compatibility facade, while keeping all newly emitted event writes strict and preserving immutable-byte transition fencing.
acceptance: trusted V2.1 validation accepts only audited already-published malformed event identities/classes required to preserve immutable historical bytes
legacy top-level review coordinates are gated by finite historical identity/provenance plus strict key/value shape; a fresh event cannot backdate itself into compatibility
the immutable historical WorldEntity review with verdict SYNC_REQUIRED validates without rewriting its bytes

the immutable MaterialDNA FINDING with legacy affects member MaterialDNA validates through an explicit finite compatibility rule, while arbitrary or newly emitted non-lane affects values still fail closed
metadata conflicts, malformed legacy values, unrelated event types, and unknown event keys remain rejected
transition-check continues to reject any historical event rewrite or deletion byte-for-byte
control deterministic/adversarial tests, canonical CI, and the live swarm-control validation path remain green before integration is declared complete
notes: PR #322 exact head 148c45f45d10f4859c87227b1bf1d698b9d78e83 was merged to main as dd8f1581115c15ce6497db827d17e98d879d0267 before independent review completed. Reviewer result evt-20260811-083400-r9v3k6-event-compat-review found three blocking gaps: timestamp-only compatibility is forgeable by fresh backdated events; known historical SYNC_REQUIRED is omitted; current live control run 31473315586 still fails immutable evt-20260811-081620-mat8c3r1-materialdna-key-grammar because affects contains MaterialDNA and the merged facade delegates that event to the strict validator. Repair main with finite historical identity/class compatibility and exact adversarial regressions; do not rewrite immutable event bytes.
